findings.reason: All three original standalone tiles show only prose and formulas. A two-row, two-column before/after switch concretely clarifies which entries decrease and increase, why all margins stay fixed, and why the orientation controls descent. This is warranted explanatory illustration under the expanded diagram scope, rather than a claim that the original proof required a figure.

diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1.3 defines the integer e-by-ell matrix with runner index 0<=i<e and component index 1<=a<=ell, row sums R_i, and column sums c_a-e. The caption uses distinct runners i,j and distinct components a,b; the figure is conditional on these choices, so it does not assert a switch exists when ell=1.

diagram_math_checks.check: Exact switch direction and unaffected entries
diagram_math_checks.justification: The arrow T(kappa) -> T(kappa prime) subtracts 1 at (i,a),(j,b), and adds 1 at (i,b),(j,a), exactly as step 1.4. The caption specifies all other entries unchanged.

For rows i,j the increments are (-1,+1) and (+1,-1); for columns a,b they are (-1,+1) and (+1,-1). Each pair sums to zero. Thus all margins stay fixed, preserving charges and hub by step 1.3; that same step guarantees the switched integer matrix represents a componentwise core.

Writing x=t_ia,y=t_ib,z=t_ja,w=t_jb gives squared norm increment (-2x+1)+(2y+1)+(2z+1)+(-2w+1)=4-2(x-y-z+w)=4-2gamma. Step 2.2 multiplies this by e/2, producing -e(gamma-2). Thus gamma=2 gives equality, and integer gamma>=3 gives strict descent; the displayed nonpositive sign assumes the stated gamma>=2 orientation.

Step 2.1 combines equal hub and equal size to obtain equal content. Accordingly the caption claims content preservation only at gamma=2; it does not mislabel strict descent as content preserving. Step 3.1 supplies the finite zero-switch and descent paths independently, and step 4.1 supplies minimum connectivity independently of this illustration.
